chunks: Say, 'O People of the Book, you have no standing until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord.' And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase in many of them transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.'
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'uphold' the Torah and Gospel according to Surah Al-Ma'idah verse 68?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the condition of validity for the People of the Book, emphasizing that their current practices are insufficient without adherence to their original scriptures and the Quran. It underscores the dialectical tension where the Quran's truth often intensifies the stubbornness of those who reject it, a theme frequently cited to explain the persistence of disbelief despite clear signs. The command for the Prophet not to grieve serves as a spiritual consolation, affirming that divine guidance is not contingent upon human acceptance.
